svg.text: Checks a customer's Kubernetes (AKS) environment against all 35 Fortanix Armor on-prem prerequisites before the install, and routes every gap to the team that can fix it
armor-preflight — one static Go binary (Linux amd64 / arm64)
no telemetry · no update check · talks only to the API server and the endpoints under test
WHERE EACH CHECK RUNS (catalog field runsIn)
read-only API calls + local tools, both modes
cluster mode only, inside the run namespace
K8S-11 LoadBalancer Service gets an IP
cluster mode only, from pods on each pool
NET-01/02/03/06/07 DNS, TCP, TLS, syslog, clock
CC-05 SGX quote · REG-03 images · BAK-02 blob

g.text: PSS restricted enforced · labelled managed-by + run-id · deleted on exit, Ctrl-C, or by `cleanup`
~2 MB static Go on distroless, UID 65532,
read-only rootfs, no caps, no SA token,
SGX probe pod × each SGX node
each probe prints one JSON line (ARMOR-PREFLIGHT-RESULT …) to its log;
the CLI reads pods/log and decides pass / fail — probes only report raw evidence
unpullable probe image → the exact digest to mirror is named; workstation checks still complete
every TLS connection is verified; a request is only sent after the chain verifies (NET-03)
at least one blocker check failed
bad settings, uncovered Armor version, internal error
• Checks run in dependency order; each level runs in parallel with a per-check timeout (default 10 s). A timeout is a fail, never a pass.
• A failed or skipped parent skips its children and names the parent (e.g. CC-05 names REG-03). Skips are per node pool: a failure on one pool never hides another.
• Warning-severity checks report warn, not fail. Missing settings or env vars skip a check and name what is missing. Every result carries evidence, fix, owning team and doc link.
